answer.rationale: The two measurable declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and memory_86 plus memory_31 both point at friction reduction as the lever that moved exactly those metrics; memory_91 corroborates that activation is movable in-product. That makes simplify_onboarding the direction best aligned with sustainable qualified revenue rather than with the loudest external stimulus. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing even though the competitor's entry pricing is the salient pressure: memory_73 records a 31% conversion and 18% revenue lift that came with a 12-point later-cycle retention loss, which is a short-horizon gain purchased against the primary objective. I spend verification on memory_86 because it is the direct basis for my chosen action and its consolidated form reports only completion and adoption -- it does not say whether the faster-completing accounts retained, converted, or were simply lower-intent, and a completion-rate lift can be a throughput artifact rather than value. I spend the second pull on memory_73 because it is the strongest counter-pull and because a consolidated summary that pairs a large headline gain with a large retention cost is exactly the kind of record whose caveats and segment scope may have been compressed away; if the retention damage was confined to a narrow cohort or was confounded by the unchanged support model, the ranking could legitimately change. I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44 because referrals target established customers and enterprise sales-assist targets a segment that is not where the decline or the competitive threat sits. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: none of these memories were measured under current competitive conditions, all are archived summaries whose original confidence intervals are unavailable to me, and it is possible the activation and onboarding declines share an upstream cause (e.g. a shift in inbound traffic mix from the competitor's entry pricing) that no onboarding change will fix. For that reason I want a standard experiment with retention and downstream qualified-revenue instrumentation, not just completion rate, and not a broad rollout on the strength of consolidated claims.
